plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Chalices of saturated colour rise on sturdy stems from the cool, damp soil of the Dutch bulb fields. Early varieties are opening into ribbons of red, yellow, pink and purple. The main show follows in the weeks after.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-May, usually at its best in mid-April
plants.location: The Netherlands (bulb-growing regions and gardens such as Keukenhof)
plants.funFact: In 17th-century Holland, tulip bulbs became so prized that single bulbs reportedly sold for more than the price of a fine townhouse. The episode is remembered as 'tulip mania'.

plants.name: Magnolia stellata
plants.description: Before a single leaf unfurls, the bare branches of this small tree burst into fragrant, many-petalled white stars. Fuzzy, pussy-willow-like buds open into ribbon-thin petals that flutter in the early spring breeze. It is one of the first real signs of the season in temperate gardens.
plants.location: Temperate gardens of North America and other cool-temperate regions (native to Japan)
plants.funFact: Magnolias belong to one of the oldest flowering plant lineages. Their blooms evolved before bees were common, so they are built tough enough to be pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Leafless stems shoot up from the bare earth, each topped with a cluster of rose-pink, trumpet-shaped, sweetly scented flowers. The blooms appear after the foliage has died back, which gives the plant its cheeky nickname. In warm, dry-summer climates the display peaks in spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in California and other warm, dry-summer regions, with blooms commonly appearing in April
plants.location: Coastal and central California gardens (native to South Africa's Western Cape)
plants.funFact: The flower stalks emerge without any leaves, so the bulbs seem to flower from bare ground. Each bulb's foliage grows in the cooler months and dies back before the flowers appear.
